themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints in Bed-Stuy surged to 4 THIS WEEK versus a baseline average of 0.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—an 700% spike (z-score: 4.95)—suggesting a potential foodborne illness cluster or contamination event requiring immediate health department investigation.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (700% increase)
Z-score of 4.95 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Department of Health and Mental Hygiene repeatedly requests increased restaurant and childcare inspection funding in budget submissions
reporting_angles: Contact DOHMH to identify which restaurants or food facilities are subject of complaints and whether outbreak investigation has been initiated
Interview affected residents about timing, symptoms, and which establishments they visited in the 24-48 hours before illness onset

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints exploded to 7 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 2700% spike (z-score: 10.21, the highest on the dataset)—indicating rapid blight accumulation or emergence of new vacant property problems across the district.
evidence: 7 lot condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (2700% increase, highest z-score: 10.21)
Highest statistical anomaly in entire 311 spike dataset
Heat/hot water (3561 complaints over 90 days) and unsanitary conditions (860) also dominate district complaints, suggesting systemic housing deterioration
reporting_angles: Identify which specific lots are driving the spike using 311 complaint geolocation; assess whether they are under same owner, subject to foreclosure, or recently abandoned
Report on whether these lots pose public health or safety risks (open dumping, structural hazards, rodent habitat); connect to spike in rodent complaints (39 last week vs. 13 avg, 200% increase)
Examine whether development pressure from five active ULURP rezonings is creating speculative abandonment

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints in Bed-Stuy jumped to 39 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 13 per week—a 200% spike (z-score: 4.1)—potentially linked to concurrent spike in lot condition complaints (7 vs. 0.2 avg) and unsanitary conditions.
evidence: 39 rodent complaints LAST WEEK vs. 13 weekly average (200% increase, z-score: 4.1)
Coincides with 2700% spike in lot condition complaints, suggesting abandoned/deteriorated properties as breeding grounds
Unsanitary condition complaints (860 over 90 days, 7th highest) remain persistently elevated
reporting_angles: Correlate 311 rodent complaints with lot condition spike to identify geographic cluster; map to specific blocks
Interview residents about severity and duration of infestation; report on whether pest control response from city has been adequate
Investigate whether lot abandonment, dumpster overflow (4 complaints last week vs. 0.6 avg, 540% spike), and reduced sanitation services are contributing factors

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Complaints Rise
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints surged to 16 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 3.1 per week—a 412% spike (z-score: 8.86)—raising questions about quality-of-life incidents, community safety perception, and police responsiveness in the district.
evidence: 16 non-emergency police complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.1 weekly baseline (412% increase, z-score: 8.86)
Second-highest z-score spike in dataset after lot condition
No corresponding Reddit discussions or local news coverage yet, suggesting emergent issue
reporting_angles: Request NYPD data on call type and response time for NYPD-linked 311 complaints; assess whether residents are filing 311 complaints in lieu of 911 calls
Interview precinct commander about staffing, quality-of-life enforcement priorities, and whether there is a specific complaint category driving the spike
Determine whether spike correlates with specific neighborhoods within Bed-Stuy or reflects district-wide trend

themes_detail.label: Obstruction & Infrastructure Decay
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints more than tripled to 12 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 3.4 per week (256% spike, z-score: 4.8), accompanied by missing street signs (3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 avg, 700% spike), suggesting street infrastructure maintenance is falling behind.
evidence: 12 obstruction complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.4 weekly baseline (256% increase, z-score: 4.8)
3 missing street sign complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Street condition complaints also elevated at 523 over 90 days (9th highest category); blocked driveways at 518
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 complaint data for obstructions to identify what is blocking streets (illegally parked vehicles, debris, construction barriers)
Investigate whether Department of Sanitation or DOT maintenance schedules have changed or been curtailed
Assess whether street sign theft/damage is localized or district-wide; connect to broader infrastructure neglect narrative
